t: From a city near Ayacucho, Wari spread planned administrative centres and colonies across highland Peru between about 600 and 1000.
Its tapestry tunics, pottery and Staff God imagery travelled widely, and feasts with maize and molle beer helped bind local leaders to the state.
The state broke up around 1000, but its roads, terraces and cord records foreshadowed the institutions of the Inca Empire.
dyk: When Wari colonists left Cerro Baúl around 1000, they held a final feast, then burned their brewery and threw their drinking cups into the flames.
ev: Wari emerges as a state in the Ayacucho basin of the central Peruvian highlands
Wari builds Pikillacta near Cusco and settles colonists on Cerro Baúl in Moquegua
Royal and noble women are buried with rich offerings at El Castillo de Huarmey
Wari officials record information on knotted and wrapped cords, early forms of the khipu
Cerro Baúl is ritually burned and abandoned as the Wari state breaks apart
Archaeologists announce an unlooted Wari mausoleum at El Castillo de Huarmey

f.successor: Chanka Confederation and other regional polities of the Late Intermediate Period
